source: Derived only from the public cases/readinglog2/README.md and BACKLOG.md. Areas are behaviors and documentation sections, not files.

rules.text: Audit log. Every successful mutating command appends exactly one JSON line to `<db>.log`: `{"op": COMMAND, "ids": [IDS in processing order], "at": UTC ISO-8601}`. Failed commands and read-only commands append nothing. (`<db>.log` is the database path with `.log` appended; a command is mutating when it can change stored books, read-only when it only reads books, even when it writes another file; `ids` is `[]` when no book was processed; `at` has a `Z` suffix; a successful mutating command saves and logs even when no book changed; the tool only appends to the log.)

Error contract. Every domain/input error prints `{"error": {"code": CODE, "message": TEXT}}` and exits 2 without any mutation. Codes come from the README's error-code table (baseline: `invalid_input`, `duplicate`, `not_found`, `storage`). A new code must be added to that table. (Usage errors included; the database and its log stay byte for byte as they were and a missing database is not created.)

Text normalization. All text input, from arguments or files, is Unicode NFC normalized, stripped, and internal whitespace runs collapse to one space. IDs are case-sensitive after normalization. (Covers IDs, titles, authors, page counts, statuses and filter values; file paths are used exactly as given; any Unicode whitespace counts; a value that must not be empty is invalid when empty after normalization; comparisons are exact after normalization.)

obligations: `finish --id ID` sets the book's status to `finished` and prints the full updated record.
Finishing a book that is already finished succeeds again and prints the same record.
`finish` with an ID that no book has fails with `not_found`.
`list --status unread|finished` lists only the books with that status, in insertion order.
Any other `--status` value fails with `invalid_input`.
`list` without `--status` is unchanged.
Tests for `finish` and `list --status` that run the CLI.
README usage and failure documentation for `finish` and `list --status`.
areas: error contract and README error-code table

rules.expectation: Every successful `finish`, including a repeated one that changes nothing, saves the database and appends exactly one line with op `finish` and ids `[ID]`. A failed `finish` and every `list` call append nothing.

Unknown ID gives `not_found`; a missing `--id`, an ID that is empty after normalization and an invalid status give `invalid_input`. All exit 2 with the error object, leave the database and log byte-identical and do not create a missing database.
`--id` and `--status` values are normalized before matching; matching is exact after normalization, so IDs and statuses are case-sensitive.

mustNotChange: the stored database format and books already stored
the audit-log line format and the `<db>.log` path

obligations: `import --csv PATH` reads a UTF-8 CSV file whose header row is exactly `id,title,author,pages`.
Every row follows the rules of `add`: nonempty ID, title and author, pages a positive integer in ASCII digits.
No ID may appear twice in the file or exist already; such an ID fails with `duplicate`.
The import is all or nothing: one invalid row rejects the whole file and changes nothing.
On success the books are appended as unread in file order and the command prints `{"imported": COUNT}`.
A file with only the header imports nothing and succeeds.
Empty lines are ignored.
A missing or unreadable file, a missing or different header, or a row with too few or too many columns fails with `invalid_input`.

rules.expectation: A successful import, including a header-only one, appends exactly one line with op `import` and the imported IDs in file order (`[]` when none). A rejected import appends nothing.
Every rejected import exits 2 with `invalid_input` or `duplicate`, leaves the database and log byte-identical and does not create a missing database.

Every CSV cell (ID, title, author, pages) is NFC-normalized, stripped and whitespace-collapsed, including line breaks inside quoted cells; duplicate detection compares normalized IDs; the `--csv` path is used exactly as given.

obligations: `summary` prints `{"authors": [{"author": NAME, "books": COUNT, "finished": COUNT, "pages": TOTAL}, ...]}`, one object per author.
Authors are ordered by name in plain code-point order.
`books` and `pages` count all of the author's books, `finished` only the finished ones.
An empty database gives `{"authors": []}`.

rules.expectation: `summary` is read-only: it appends no log line, never changes the database and does not create a missing one.
Unknown options of `summary` fail with `invalid_input`; a malformed database fails with `storage`.
Books group by their stored, normalized author; the order compares code points of those names.

obligations: Regression tests for the baseline commands and for `finish`, `list --status`, `import` and `summary`.
README usage documentation for the new commands.
README failure documentation: which errors the new commands report.
README stored-state documentation: what the new commands store and what they leave unchanged.
areas: README error documentation and error-code table

rules.expectation: The README error-code table lists every code the CLI emits.

obligations: `list --author NAME` lists only that author's books, in insertion order.
`--author` combines with `--status`.
areas: command list: --author filter and filter combination

rules.expectation: `list --author` appends nothing and never changes the database.
The author filter value is normalized; matching is exact after normalization (case-sensitive).

obligations: `export --csv PATH` writes every book to a UTF-8 CSV file with the header `id,title,author,pages,status` (plus the `tags` column of B08), in insertion order, with standard CSV quoting.
`export` prints `{"exported": COUNT}`.
`export` never changes the database.
A destination that cannot be written fails with the new error code `export_failed`.
`export_failed` is added to the README error-code table.
areas: error contract and README error-code table

rules.expectation: `export` is read-only even though it writes a file: no log line, the database is unchanged and a missing database is not created.
An unwritable destination exits 2 with `export_failed` and no mutation; `export_failed` appears in the README error-code table; a missing `--csv` is `invalid_input`.
The `--csv` path is used exactly as given.

mustNotChange: the database file and its log

obligations: `summary --author NAME` reports only that author.
An unknown author gives `{"authors": []}`.
`summary` without `--author` stays unchanged.

rules.expectation: `summary --author` is read-only.
The author value is normalized; matching is exact after normalization.

obligations: `tag --id ID --add TAG` or `tag --id ID --remove TAG`, exactly one of the two, changes one book's tags and prints the updated record.
Adding a tag the book already has, or removing one it does not have, succeeds without a change.
Records gain the field `tags`: the book's distinct tags in code-point order, `[]` for new books (added or imported).
A tag is nonempty, may not contain `;` and is case-sensitive; an invalid tag is `invalid_input`; an unknown ID is `not_found`.
`list --tag TAG` lists only books with that tag and combines with every other `list` filter.
`export` gains a last column `tags` holding the book's tags joined by `;`.
Books stored before tags existed stay readable as books without tags, and reading them never rewrites the file.
areas: command list: --tag filter and filter combination

rules.expectation: Every successful `tag`, including one that changes nothing, appends exactly one line with op `tag` and ids `[ID]`; failed `tag` and `list --tag` append nothing.
Neither or both of `--add`/`--remove`, an empty tag and a tag with `;` give `invalid_input`, an unknown ID gives `not_found`; no mutation.
Tag values from `--add`, `--remove` and `--tag` are normalized; tags compare exactly after normalization (case-sensitive).

mustNotChange: stored books written before tags existed (no rewrite on read)
existing list filters and their order

obligations: Query tests: filter combinations and order across processes.
Export tests: quoting, tags column, empty database, unchanged database and an unwritable destination.
Reporting tests: summary for one author and for unknown authors.
Tags tests: repeated tagging, unknown IDs, invalid tags and books stored without tags.
All four groups are integrated on `main` with regression tests.
README docs for `list --author`, `export`, `summary --author`, `tag`, `list --tag`, the tags field and `export_failed`.
TEAMWORK.md records the real team: identities, time intervals, commit SHAs, merges and conflicts.
At least two executing agents overlapped in time on independent groups and both contributions are merged.
areas: README usage, records and error-code table

rules.expectation: The README error-code table lists every code the CLI emits, including `export_failed`.

obligations: The database file becomes `{"schemaVersion": 2, "records": [...]}`.
Files in the version 1 array format stay readable by every command.
Read-only commands never rewrite a file, in either format.
The first successful mutation writes version 2, also for a version 1 file and also when it changes no book.
Command output stays unchanged and is the same for both formats.
areas: every command reading version 1 and version 2 files
audit log on the first mutation

rules.expectation: The mutation that upgrades a version 1 file appends exactly the one line of that command (its own op and ids), nothing else; read-only commands on a version 1 file append nothing.
A failed command on a version 1 file leaves it byte-identical (still version 1); a malformed version 2 file fails every command with `storage` and is never overwritten.

obligations: Tests that run every command against version 1 files.
README documentation of both storage formats.
A book may have an unknown page count, stored and shown as `"pages": null`.
`add` without `--pages` or with an empty value stores an unknown page count.
An empty `pages` cell in an import file stores an unknown page count.
A given page count must still be a positive integer in ASCII digits.
`summary` (with and without `--author`) sums only known pages and reports `unknownPages` per author, the number of the author's books without a page count.
`export` writes an unknown page count as an empty cell.
Unknown page counts are accepted in both storage formats and survive later changes such as `finish` and `tag`.
areas: record shape and storage validation for null pages

rules.expectation: `add` without pages and `import` with empty pages cells append their normal single line.
A given but invalid page count (zero, negative, signed, decimal, non-ASCII digits) still fails with `invalid_input` and no mutation.
A page value that is empty after normalization (for example only whitespace) means unknown.

mustNotChange: the other summary fields and their order

obligations: Tests for unknown page counts across every affected command (add, import, summary, summary --author, export, list) and both storage formats.
README documentation of optional pages, `null` and `unknownPages`.
areas: README usage, records and storage documentation

obligations: The active domain term book becomes entry in interfaces, code, tests and docs.
`list` responds `{"entries": [...]}` and each `summary` author object counts `entries` instead of `books`.
`--legacy` on `list` and `summary` returns exactly the previous response shape for one compatibility period.
`--legacy` combines with all filters of that command: `--status`, `--author` and `--tag` for `list`, `--author` for `summary`.
Stored data, audit-log operation names and CSV headers stay unchanged.
The compatibility plan is explained before it is implemented.
Tests of the new and the legacy shapes against data written before the rename, in both storage formats.

rules.expectation: Audit lines keep the op names `add`, `finish`, `import` and `tag`.
Error codes are unchanged; `--legacy` with an invalid filter value still fails with `invalid_input`.
Filter values combined with `--legacy` are normalized like without it.

mustNotChange: stored data in both formats (`schemaVersion`, `records`, record fields)
CSV headers of import and export
responses that did not say books (records, imported, exported, error objects)
